Subject: Inference deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & topology for Cambridge Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive next week.

1) Main pain / goals (as we understood them)
- Patient-facing triage service needs sub-200ms median and <=120ms p95 for short prompts (few-shot summaries, symptom extraction).
- Peak load ~180–220 QPS during business hours (multi-region failover).
- Strict data controls: HIPAA, customer-managed keys, audit logs for every inference.
- Prefer private/VPC deployment but want hosted fallback for burst to avoid dropped requests.

2) Model & inference requirements we discussed
- Primary model: 8k context LLM for summarization + extraction; team indicated preference toward a 13B–70B family depending on accuracy tradeoffs.
- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with embeddings lookup (approx 1 embedding call per 3 requests on average).
- Strong desire to use 4-bit quantization for cost; confirm accuracy/regression risk with evaluations.

3) Target SLOs (draft, confirm with you)
- P95 token latency <= 120ms for single-turn 64-token outputs (interactive paths).
- Median token latency < 50ms.
- Availability SLO: 99.95% in-region; cross-region failover within 30s.
- Cost goal: keep hosted equivalent unit cost within 30% of current internal benchmarks.

4) Deployment topology options we recommend to test (high level)
- Private Redwood deployment (VPC) with dedicated capacity for primary traffic + autoscaling; KV/prefix caching enabled in front of model to reduce cold-starts.
- Multi-variant routing: prefer low-latency model (quantized 70B or 13B distil) for production, automatic fallback to smaller model during contention.
- Optional burst routing to Redwood hosted (encrypted, short-lived tokens) for unexpected peaks.

Attachments: attached a short SLO table and a topology sketch (slo_summary_table.csv; topology_sketch.png).

Next steps / asks (action items)
- Priya: confirm which environment (VPC-only vs private+hosted fallback) is required for the procurement team and desired timeline.
- Cambridge security: share the standard security questionnaire PDF so we can map controls to the Private offering.
- Internal (Karthik): run a back-of-envelope capacity estimate for 180–220 QPS for 13B vs 70B quantized variants (include burst headroom).
- Internal (Irene): list the required artifacts for HIPAA + SOC2 evidence and whether HSM integration is mandatory.

I’ll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next Wed/Thu — invite to follow once you confirm availability. Thanks again — enjoyed the discussion.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — this is helpful and aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Procurement timeline: our vendor committee meets July 8; ideal go/no-go decision by end of July so we can start pilot in August.
- Security: we require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for PHI encrypt-at-rest and a SOC2 Type II attestation.
- Quantization question: we’re open to 4-bit if you can show parity on key NLU tasks (extraction precision). Will need a short eval on our prompts.
- Failover: hosted burst is acceptable but must guarantee no PHI persists outside our VPC — tokens must be ephemeral and logs redacted.

One ask: can you confirm whether the latency numbers you quoted assume local KV cache hits? Our worst-case numbers are when the RAG retrieval adds 40–60ms for DB lookups (we might front with an in-memory vector cache).

Happy to take the deep-dive on Wed 23rd 10:00–11:00 PT if that works for your team.

Mina / Irene — quick answers and a couple of assumptions we used. Attached: capacity_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet stub) and karthik_burst_calc.pdf (one-page calc).

Assumptions
- Target QPS: 200 steady with 30% burst to 260 QPS.
- Typical output length: 64 tokens; 8–10 kb context average for retrieval; 1.2 embedding calls per request (RAG amortized).
- Hardware: H100 80GB (preferred) and fallback to A100 80GB in some zones. 70B 4-bit LLAMA-style quantization requires ~40–48GB GPU working set with KV/cache management; fits on a single H100 but tight on A100 depending on kernel memory. 13B quantized fits comfortably with more headroom.

Rough fleet sizing (steady / effective)
- 70B (4-bit) variant: ~6 H100s to meet steady 200 QPS with target p95 latency band (caching and batching enabled). Add 2–3 nodes for 30% burst headroom (total 8–9).
- 13B (4-bit) variant: ~2 H100s steady; add 1 node for burst (total 3).

Cost note (very rough monthly run-rate)
- 70B Private dedicated (8 nodes): material uplift vs 13B dedicated (3 nodes) driven by GPU hours + memory pressure; estimate ~2.8–3.5x cost multiplier. Final pricing will depend on reserved commit.

Security / KMS notes
- We support customer-managed KMS in Private; HSM deployments require lead time (2–4 weeks) for provisioning and key exchange with the customer’s security team. We can redaction/filter logs before they leave the VPC if required (configurable).

Next steps I’ll take before Monday:
- Populate the capacity_estimate.xlsx with per-model per-node QPS, expected p95 latencies for cold/warm hit rates, and cost delta.
- Flag potential perf/regression risk for 4-bit 70B and suggest a short accuracy run on Priya’s sample prompts (we can run evaluation on our dev infra).

If you want, I can join the Wed 23rd call to walk the numbers.
